title: Justice in Healthcare Artificial Intelligence in Africa

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical discussion and literature review regarding the reinforcement of gender stereotypes and the exacerbation of healthcare inequities for women and girls in Africa due to underrepresentation in training data.

Analysis of the disproportionate representation of population subgroups in biomedical databases, specifically the underrepresentation of African populations and overrepresentation of individuals of European descent.
Discussion of how inappropriate combination of population data (e.g., combining urban and rural data) masks within-group differences and health disparities in the African context.
Examination of the risks where synthetic data generation techniques inherit and propagate biases from models trained on non-representative (Western) datasets.
Evaluation of fairness implications when AI models trained on data from high-income countries are deployed in African healthcare settings with different population characteristics.
Discussion of how the digital divide and unequal access to AI technologies can amplify existing socioeconomic inequalities and health disparities.
